author: NorthEast News Desk
body: UBS will shut down its independent fund-distribution business in Shenzhen at the end of September, four years after launching the platform for affluent investors in China.

The Swiss bank said the unit, branded WE.UBS, will stop fund sales and that relevant resources will be integrated elsewhere. UBS emphasized that its other wealth-management platforms in China are operating normally.

Three people familiar with the operation told Reuters that WE.UBS struggled to scale in a highly competitive market and also faced overlap with other UBS businesses. The bank’s brokerage and banking units in China already hold licenses that allow them to sell funds.

The closure narrows one part of UBS’s China retail-distribution strategy without amounting to a withdrawal from the broader market. For investors, the development highlights the challenge foreign financial firms face in building standalone digital-sales platforms while competing with domestic providers and their own licensed subsidiaries. UBS did not disclose the platform’s assets, customer count or expected financial impact.
dek: The Swiss bank said its WE.UBS platform will stop selling funds at the end of September while its other China wealth businesses continue.
headline: UBS to close China fund-distribution platform after four years
